To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
C1‐IN‐L is present on human sperm and that its binding to sperm is associated with sperm motility.
a 88–92 kDa molecule, which is similar to human C1‐INHL, is present on the surface of spermatozoa, and its level is significantly lower in infertile patients than in fertile controls.
the presence of a C1INH‐L molecule on the human sperm membrane can be detected by a human IgG fraction of anti‐C1INH antibody, and that it is capable of inhibiting sperm motility in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a C1 inhibitor‐like protein on human sperm.
the presence of a C1 inhibitor‐like molecule (CIINHL) in human seminal plasma.
the identification of a C1 inhibitor-like molecule on the surface of human sperm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of a 88–92 kDa C1‐IN‐L on the sperm surface may be involved in the regulation of sperm motility and that the C1‐INL‐like protein on sperm surface may be an important target of sperm‐autoantibody response in the immunologic infertility.
C1‐INL‐L is present on human sperm and is involved in the regulation of sperm motility.
the C1‐IN‐H‐L molecule on the sperm surface is involved in sperm motility and its presence on the surface is associated with sperm function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that C1‐INL, a protein that was originally identified in the serum of infertile women and in the seminal plasma of infertile men, is also present on the human ejaculated sperm surface.
C1‐INHL is a sperm surface molecule, and that it is involved in sperm motility, but not in acrosome reaction.
C1‐IN‐L is a sperm surface molecule that can be identified by an anti‐human C‐IN‐H antibody, and it can be involved in human sperm motility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C1‐INHL molecule is present on the sperm surface.
the C1‐INL molecule is a novel sperm surface molecule that is involved in the control of sperm motility.
C1‐IN‐L is present on human sperm and could be detected on sperm surface by anti‐human C‐INH IgG antibody.
